---
title: "Exploring observed curves"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`viewcurves()` opens an app to step through the observed curves of the individuals of a data set:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(gcTMB)
viewcurves(FabaHeights26, x = "DAS", y = "Height", id = "Plant_ID", covariates = c("Genotype", "Soil"),
           output = "html")
```

The app below is that call, running in your browser. It can take half a minute to start the first time,
and it responds more slowly than the app does when `viewcurves()` is run in R on your own computer.

```{=html}
<iframe src="../viewcurves-app/index.html" title="viewcurves() app" width="100%" height="1050"
        style="border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px;" loading="lazy"></iframe>
```

## Outliers in the data

With `output = "jpeg"`, `viewcurves()` draws the curves and growth rates of all plants. The plants with
the steepest increases and the plants with the steepest decreases between two measurements, `outliers`
of each, are drawn in red and reported:

```{r, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5, message = TRUE}
library(gcTMB)
vc <- viewcurves(FabaHeights26, x = "DAS", y = "Height", id = "Plant_ID", covariates = c("Genotype", "Soil"),
                 output = "jpeg", outliers = 3)
```

## Outliers in the residuals

The validation plots of a fitted model draw the `outliers` observations with the largest absolute
residuals in red, labelled by their plant, here for a logistic curve with random effects of the plants on the asymptote
b1 and the inflection point b2:

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform = b1 + b2 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, truncated = FALSE, data = FabaHeights26)
plot(fit, outliers = 3)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
r <- residuals(fit, type = "normalized")
resid_ids <- unique(as.character(fit$data$Plant_ID[order(abs(r), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]]))
data_ids <- unique(vc$outliers$id)
both <- intersect(data_ids, resid_ids)
only_data <- setdiff(data_ids, resid_ids)
only_resid <- setdiff(resid_ids, data_ids)
words <- function(x) if (length(x) == 1) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
found <- c(
  if (length(both) > 0) paste0("Both methods flag ", words(both), "."),
  if (length(only_data) > 0) paste0("Only the data flag ", words(only_data), "."),
  if (length(only_resid) > 0) paste0("Only the residuals flag ", words(only_resid), "."))
```

The two kinds of outliers are not the same. A steep rise or fall in the data is not unusual for a
plant whose own fitted curve rises or falls steeply there, while a residual measures how far an
observation is from the curve of its plant. `r paste(found, collapse = " ")`
